[[File:Halocnemum strobilaceum.jpg|thumb|right|''Halocnemum strobilaceum'']]

'''''Halocnemum strobilaceum''''' is a [[species]] of flowering plant in the subfamily [[Salicornioideae]] of the family [[Amaranthaceae]]. It is native to coastal areas of the [[Mediterranean Sea]] and the [[Red Sea]] and parts of the [[Middle East]] and central Asia, where it grows in coastal and inland [[salt marsh]]es, [[Dry lake|alkali flats]], and other habitats with [[Soil salinity|saline soils]].

==Description==
''Halocnemum strobilaceum'' is a much-branched, semi-prostrate, sub-shrub with erect branches up to a metre or so high. The woody stems at the base are jointed and have sterile, rounded or conical shaped buds, arranged in whorls on the terminal part of each portion. The erect stems are  cylindrical and succulent, with green joints that turn yellow as they age. The stubby, bluish-green, scale-like leaves clasp the stem at each node. The flowers are [[hermaphrodite]] and very small, and are arranged in whorls of three on the upper part of the branches.<ref name=Grigore>{{cite book|author1=Grigore, Marius-Nicusor |author2=Ivanescu, Lacramioara |author3= Toma, Constantin |title=Halophytes: An Integrative Anatomical Study |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pOEkBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA175 |year= 2014 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-05729-3 |pages=175–177}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Halocnemum strobilaceum'' is found around the coasts bordering on the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea. It is also present in the Middle East and central Asia as far east as [[Mongolia]] and China. In Iran and Pakistan, it grows in the muddy coastal swamps immediately inland from the mangroves (''[[Avicennia marina]]'') that border the coast of the Persian Gulf.<ref name=Ahmad>{{cite book|author1=Ahmad, R.|author2=Malik, K.A.|title=Prospects for Saline Agriculture |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6s3rCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA353 |year=2013 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-94-017-0067-2 |pages=353–363}}</ref> In the delta region of the Mediterranean coast of Egypt, it dominates some plant communities in the [[salt marsh]] habitats.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Zahran, M.A. |author2=El-Demerdash, M.A. |author3=Mashaly, I.A. |year=1990 |title=Vegetation types of the deltaic Mediterranean coast of Egypt and their environment |journal=Journal of Vegetation Science |volume=1 |issue=3 |pages=305–310 |doi=10.2307/3235705 |jstor=3235705 |bibcode=1990JVegS...1..305Z }}</ref> In [[Abu Dhabi]] it grows in lagoons with muddy substrates in association with ''[[Arthrocnemum macrostachyum]]'', and along the storm ridges of shelly sand that form higher up the beach. Gelatinous crusts of [[cyanobacteria]] sometimes form in depressions in the ground, and when these get dusted with windblown sand, ''H. strobilaceum'' colonises these habitats too.<ref name=Khan>{{cite book|author1=Khan, M. Ajmal |author2=Böer, Benno |author3=Kust, German S. |author4=Barth, Hans-Jörg |title=Sabkha Ecosystems: Volume II: West and Central Asia|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IYVGAAAAQBAJ&pg=PA42 |year=2008 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-1-4020-5072-5 |page=42}}</ref> It grows along the sandy [[Tunisia]]n coast, forming hummocks, growing alongside [[Bassia muricata]], [[Cutandia memphitica]] and [[Traganum nudatum]].<ref>R. H. Hughes {{google books|VLjafeXa3gMC|A Directory of African Wetlands|page=5}}</ref>

In northwestern China in the provinces of [[Xinjiang]] and [[Gansu]], it is one of the dominant plants on saline plains, on the shores of salt lakes and at the edges of alluvial fans.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Xiao-Xia Qu |author2=Zhen-Ying Huang |author3=Jerry M. Baskin |author4=Carol C. Baskin |year=2007 |title=Effect of Temperature, Light and Salinity on Seed Germination and Radicle Growth of the Geographically Widespread Halophyte Shrub ''Halocnemum strobilaceum'' |journal=Annals of Botany |volume=101 |issue=2 |pages=293–299 |doi=10.1093/aob/mcm047 |pmid=17428834 |pmc=2711011}}</ref> Along with [[Salicornia europaea|glasswort]] and ''A. macrostachyum'', ''H. strobilaceum'' was one of the first plants to recolonise oil-polluted marshland in the Persian Gulf after the soil had been churned up and aerated by the action of [[crab]]s.<ref name=Abuzinada>{{cite book|author1=Abdulaziz H. Abuzinada |author2=Hans-Jörg Barth |author3=Friedhelm Krupp |author4=Benno Böer Thabit |author5=Zahran Al Abdessalaam |title=Protecting the Gulf's Marine Ecosystems from Pollution|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8vMzKsGikTkC&pg=PA270 |year=2008 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-7643-7947-6 |page=270}}</ref>
